body.statement:
For every \(P\in\mathcal F_s\) and every smooth four-density path with tangent \(\delta\), the selected lifted map \(P\mapsto(\widetilde T(\widetilde y_j))_{j=1}^J\) is Fr\'echet differentiable and its derivative is exactly the corrected operator \(\mathcal D_P[\delta]\) in def:nested-derivative.  Explicitly, its harmonic part is
\[
\mathcal H_P[\delta]
=\left(
b_T+\nabla\mathcal L_B^{-1}\Pi_0\!\left[
\operatorname{div}(B b_T)
-(\mathsf C\nabla\alpha)\cdot\left(
b_p+\nabla\mathcal L_{\mathsf C}^{-1}\Pi_0
\operatorname{div}(\mathsf C b_p)
\right)
\right]
\right)_{\mathcal Y_J},
\]
where \(b_p=\dot a_p\) and \(b_T=\dot a_T\) are determined by the differentiated reduced-cost stationarity equations.  The remaining scalar part is
\[
\left(
\nabla\mathcal L_B^{-1}\Pi_0
[\alpha(e_{C1}-e_{C0})+e_{T0}-e_{T1}]
-\nabla\mathcal L_B^{-1}\Pi_0\!\left[
(\mathsf C\nabla\alpha)\cdot
\nabla\mathcal L_{\mathsf C}^{-1}\Pi_0(e_{C1}-e_{C0})
\right]
\right)_{\mathcal Y_J}.
\]
The coefficient identity \(BD^{-\mathsf T}=\alpha\mathsf C\) holds.  The two augmented scalar--harmonic systems are uniformly invertible over \(\mathcal F_s\), and the maps \(\delta\mapsto(b_p,b_T)\) have cellwise Riesz scores with uniformly bounded \(L^2(P_g)\) norms.  Consequently \(\mathcal H_P\) contributes \(O(1/\log(1/h))\) to \(\Sigma_h(P)\), and its cross-covariance with the Green score is \(O(1/\sqrt{\log(1/h)})\), uniformly over \(\mathcal F_s\).  This extends the one-target fixed-source density-curve derivative in GonzalezSanzSheng2024Linearization to a four-input nested map with a generated target law and nonzero harmonic translation modes.
body.justification: The weighted-Hodge Schur complement proves uniform harmonic invertibility, determines both nonzero translation derivatives, and yields the exact corrected four-input decomposition.
body.gap: The frozen formula omitted the scalar elliptic correctors generated by the inner and outer harmonic velocities; this bundle supplies the required formal correction and proof without a new assumption.
body.consumer: Every finite-bandwidth score and adjoint implementation must use the corrected coefficient-divergence terms.
body.proof_tex:
Write \(f=f_{C0}\), \(g=f_{C1}\) for the inner problem.  We first establish the scalar--harmonic linearization for a generic selected no-cut transport
\[
F(x)=x+a+\nabla\phi(x),\qquad F\#(f\,dx)=g\,dx,
\tag{1}
\]
where \(\phi\) is periodic with zero Lebesgue mean.  By ass:density-positivity and the relevant one of ass:inner-ellipticity and ass:outer-ellipticity, \(f\geq c\) and
\[
\lambda I_2\preceq DF\preceq\Lambda I_2.
\tag{2}
\]
Thus
\[
A_F:=f(DF)^{-1}\quad\hbox{satisfies}\quad
\frac c\Lambda I_2\preceq A_F\preceq\frac C\lambda I_2.
\tag{3}
\]
In particular, \(-\operatorname{div}(A_F\nabla\cdot)\) is invertible on mean-zero periodic functions: if its right-hand side is \(r\) with \(\int r=0\), testing the weak equation by its solution and using (3) and the periodic Poincar\'e inequality gives
\[
\lVert\nabla u\rVert_2
\leq C\lVert r\rVert_{H^{-1}}.
\tag{4}
\]

The finite-dimensional equation is supplied by optimality, not by the mass equation.  On the fixed smooth cost chart guaranteed by ass:lift-regularity, introduce the Kantorovich Lagrangian
\[
\mathcal K(F,\eta)
=\frac12\int_{\mathbb T^2}|F(x)-x|^2f(x)\,dx
+\int_{\mathbb T^2}\eta(F(x))f(x)\,dx
-\int_{\mathbb T^2}\eta(y)g(y)\,dy.
\tag{5}
\]
Stationarity in \(F\) gives
\[
\nabla\eta(F(x))=x-F(x).
\tag{6}
\]
Differentiating (6) with respect to \(x\), and using the symmetry and invertibility of \(DF\), yields
\[
I_2+D^2\eta(F(x))=(DF(x))^{-1}.
\tag{7}
\]

Fix \(b\in\mathbb R^2\).  A variation of the selected lift having harmonic velocity \(b\) has the form
\[
v_b=b+\nabla\psi_b,qquad \int_{\mathbb T^2}\psi_b=0.
\tag{8}
\]
Differentiating \(g(F)\det DF=f\) with \(f,g\) held fixed, and using the Piola identity, gives
\[
\operatorname{div}(A_Fv_b)=0,
\qquad
-\operatorname{div}(A_F\nabla\psi_b)
=\operatorname{div}(A_Fb).
\tag{9}
\]
Equation (4) makes \(\psi_b\) unique.  The second constrained variation of (5) has no acceleration term because the first-order Lagrange equations hold.  Equations (7)--(9) therefore give the reduced-cost Hessian identity
\[
b^{\mathsf T}D^2J_F(a)b
=\int_{\mathbb T^2}
v_b^{\mathsf T}A_Fv_b
=\inf_{\substack{\psi\ \mathrm{periodic}\\ \int\psi=0}}
\int_{\mathbb T^2}
(b+\nabla\psi)^{\mathsf T}A_F(b+\nabla\psi).
\tag{10}
\]
Indeed, (9) is exactly the Euler equation for the displayed strictly convex energy, and hence proves the second equality.  Since \(\int_{\mathbb T^2}\nabla\psi=0\), (3) gives
\[
b^{\mathsf T}D^2J_F(a)b
\geq\frac c\Lambda
\int_{\mathbb T^2}|b+\nabla\psi_b|^2
=\frac c\Lambda\left(|b|^2+\lVert\nabla\psi_b\rVert_2^2\right)
\geq\frac c\Lambda|b|^2.
\tag{11}
\]
This is the required uniform harmonic coercivity; no harmonic nondegeneracy assumption has been added.

Now let \((f_t,g_t)\) be a smooth density path and put \((\dot f,\dot g)=\partial_t(f_t,g_t)|_0\).  If
\[
\dot F=b_F+\nabla u_F,qquad \int u_F=0,
\tag{12}
\]
then differentiating the mass identity gives
\[
\dot f
=\det(DF)\dot g\circ F
+\operatorname{div}\{A_F(b_F+\nabla u_F)\}.
\tag{13}
\]
Consequently, with \(r_F=\det(DF)\dot g\circ F-\dot f\),
\[
-\operatorname{div}(A_F\nabla u_F)
=r_F+\operatorname{div}(A_Fb_F).
\tag{14}
\]
The right-hand side has zero integral, so (4) applies.

To display the second equation, let \(J_F(a;f,g)\) be the reduced cost obtained by solving the scalar mass equation at fixed \(a\), and define the well-typed density-forcing vector
\[
c^{\mathsf T}\mathfrak s_F[\dot f,\dot g]
:=\left.\frac d{dt}\right|_{t=0}
D_aJ_F(a;f_t,g_t)[c],qquad c\in\mathbb R^2.
\tag{15}
\]
Differentiating \(D_aJ_F(a_t;f_t,g_t)=0\) and using (10) gives
\[
D^2J_F(a)b_F=-\mathfrak s_F[\dot f,\dot g],
\qquad
b_F=-\{D^2J_F(a)\}^{-1}\mathfrak s_F[\dot f,\dot g].
\tag{16}
\]
Equations (4), (11), (14), and (16) prove invertibility of the augmented scalar--harmonic system.

For later stochastic use, we record continuity of the forcing in (15).  Differentiate (5) once in the density path and once in the harmonic direction \(c\).  Terms containing derivatives of the constrained map cancel by (6) and the differentiated constraint (13).  The remaining terms are finite sums of (i) integrals of \(\dot f\) and \(\dot g\) against the smooth functions \(F-x\), \(\eta\), and their pullbacks, and (ii) the energy pairing
\[
\int_{\mathbb T^2}v_c^{\mathsf T}A_F\nabla u_0,
\qquad
-\operatorname{div}(A_F\nabla u_0)=r_F,
\tag{17}
\]
where \(|c|=1\).  The smooth coefficients are uniformly bounded on the class, (4) bounds \(\nabla u_0\), and (10)--(11) bound \(v_c\).  After changing variables by \(F\), Cauchy--Schwarz gives
\[
|\mathfrak s_F[\dot f,\dot g]|
\leq C\left(
\left\lVert\frac{\dot f}{f}\right\rVert_{L^2(f)}
+\left\lVert\frac{\dot g}{g}\right\rVert_{L^2(g)}
\right).
\tag{18}
\]
Combining (11), (16), and (18) gives the same bound for \(|b_F|\).  Solving the two adjoint equations associated with (14) and the two columns of (16), and then integrating by parts in (15), writes every coordinate of \(b_F\) as
\[
\sum_{e\in\{f,g\}}\int_{\mathbb T^2}\zeta_{F,e}(x)\dot e(x)\,dx,
\qquad
\sup_{F,e}\lVert\zeta_{F,e}\rVert_{L^2(e)}<\infty.
\tag{19}
\]
Thus (19) is an explicit adjoint construction of the asserted bounded Riesz scores, rather than an assumption about them.

Apply (12)--(16) first to \(p\).  Put \(b_p=\dot a_p\), write \(u_p\) for its scalar derivative, and set
\[
r_p=\det(S)\delta_{C1}\circ p-\delta_{C0}.
\tag{20}
\]
Then
\[
\mathcal L_Au_p=r_p+\operatorname{div}(Ab_p).
\tag{21}
\]
In treated-post coordinates define the mean-zero representative of
\[
\bar u_p(y)=b_p^{\mathsf T}\{R_0(y)-y\}+u_p(R_0(y)).
\tag{22}
\]
Because \(R_0\) is identity-homotopic, the right-hand side is periodic up to an irrelevant additive constant.  The chain rule gives
\[
b_p+\nabla\bar u_p(y)
=D(y)^{\mathsf T}\{b_p+\nabla u_p(R_0(y))\}.
\tag{23}
\]
Changing variables in (21) by \(R_0\), using the Piola identity and the definitions of the transformed noises, gives
\[
\mathcal L_{\mathsf C}\bar u_p
=e_{C1}-e_{C0}+\operatorname{div}(\mathsf Cb_p).
\tag{24}
\]
The term \(\operatorname{div}(\mathsf Cb_p)\) is forced by the harmonic velocity and cannot be discarded when \(\mathsf C\) is nonconstant.

Differentiate the generated target exactly.  For every smooth periodic test function \(\zeta\),
\[
\left.\frac d{dt}\right|_0\int\zeta\,dq_t
=\int\zeta(p(x))\delta_{T0}(x)\,dx
+\int\nabla\zeta(p(x))^{\mathsf T}\{b_p+\nabla u_p(x)\}f_{T0}(x)\,dx.
\tag{25}
\]
Integration by parts after the change of variables \(z=p(x)\) yields
\[
\dot q=p\#\delta_{T0}
-\operatorname{div}_z\!\left[q(z)\{b_p+\nabla u_p\}(p^{-1}(z))\right].
\tag{26}
\]
Pulling (26) through \(T\) and then using (23) gives
\[
\det(H)\dot q\circ T
=e_{T0}-\operatorname{div}_y\!\left[
BD^{-\mathsf T}\{b_p+\nabla\bar u_p\}
\right].
\tag{27}
\]

We next prove the matrix identity used to reduce (27).  The population mass identities imply
\[
f_{T1}(y)=f_{T0}(R_0(y))\det D(y).
\tag{28}
\]
Since \(D=S(R_0)^{-1}H\), while \(S\) and \(H\) are symmetric,
\[
\begin{aligned}
\alpha\mathsf C
&=\frac{f_{T0}(R_0)}{f_{C0}(R_0)}
\det(D)D^{-1}\{f_{C0}(R_0)S(R_0)^{-1}\}D^{-\mathsf T}\\
&=f_{T0}(R_0)\det(D)H^{-1}S(R_0)H^{-1}\\
&=f_{T1}H^{-1}S(R_0)H^{-1}
=BD^{-\mathsf T}.
\end{aligned}
\tag{29}
\]
No commutativity of \(S\) and \(H\) was used.

Equations (24), (27), and (29), together with the product rule, imply
\[
\begin{aligned}
\det(H)\dot q\circ T
&=e_{T0}-\operatorname{div}\!\left[
\alpha\mathsf C\{b_p+\nabla\bar u_p\}
\right]\\
&=e_{T0}+\alpha(e_{C1}-e_{C0})
-(\mathsf C\nabla\alpha)\cdot
\{b_p+\nabla\bar u_p\}.
\end{aligned}
\tag{30}
\]
Apply the generic augmented system a second time to \(T\).  With \(b_T=\dot a_T\) and scalar derivative \(u_T\), equations (14) and (30) give
\[
\mathcal L_Bu_T
=e_{T0}-e_{T1}+\alpha(e_{C1}-e_{C0})
-(\mathsf C\nabla\alpha)\cdot
\{b_p+\nabla\bar u_p\}
+\operatorname{div}(Bb_T).
\tag{31}
\]
By linearity of (24),
\[
\nabla\bar u_p
=\nabla\mathcal L_{\mathsf C}^{-1}\Pi_0(e_{C1}-e_{C0})
+\nabla\mathcal L_{\mathsf C}^{-1}\Pi_0
\operatorname{div}(\mathsf Cb_p).
\tag{32}
\]
Substituting (32) into (31), applying \(\nabla\mathcal L_B^{-1}\Pi_0\), and adding \(b_T\) proves exactly the corrected formulas for \(\mathcal H_P\) and \(\mathcal D_P\).  In particular, both \(\operatorname{div}(\mathsf Cb_p)\) and \(\operatorname{div}(Bb_T)\) are retained.

For completeness, we prove Fr\'echet rather than merely pathwise differentiability.  Let \(u=(u_g)_{g\in\mathcal G}\) be a zero-integral density perturbation, fix \(\vartheta=1/4\), and put
\[
U_1=\max_g\lVert u_g\rVert_{C^{1,\vartheta}},
\qquad
U_0=\max_g\lVert u_g\rVert_{C^{0,\vartheta}}.
\tag{33}
\]
Assume only for this local expansion that the \(C^{2,\vartheta}\) norm is small enough to remain in the branch chart; ass:lift-regularity supplies one common chart radius.  The nonlinear identities needed by the two augmented implicit systems are, in dimension two,
\[
\det(M+E)-\det M-\operatorname{cof}(M):E=\det E,
\tag{34}
\]
and, whenever \(a\geq c\) and \(|v|\leq c/2\),
\[
\frac1{a+v}-\frac1a+\frac v{a^2}
=\frac{v^2}{a^2(a+v)}.
\tag{35}
\]
The product rule in H\"older spaces applied to (34)--(35) gives
\[
\lVert R_{\det}\rVert_{C^{0,\vartheta}}
+\lVert R_{\mathrm{recip}}\rVert_{C^{0,\vartheta}}
\leq CU_1U_0.
\tag{36}
\]
For composition, the integral identity
\[
q(x+v)-q(x)-Dq(x)v
=\int_0^1\{Dq(x+tv)-Dq(x)\}v\,dt
\tag{37}
\]
and the differentiated identity for the inverse map give
\[
\lVert R_{\mathrm{comp}}\rVert_{C^{0,\vartheta}}
+\lVert R_{\mathrm{inv}}\rVert_{C^{0,\vartheta}}
\leq CU_1U_0.
\tag{38}
\]
Here the higher factor controls one derivative of a density or map increment and the lower factor controls its amplitude.  Differentiating (5) on the same chart and using (34)--(38) shows that the residual in the finite-dimensional stationarity equation satisfies
\[
|R_{\mathrm{harm}}|\leq CU_1U_0.
\tag{39}
\]
The inverse bound (4) for the scalar block and (11) for its weighted-Hodge Schur complement transform (36)--(39) into
\[
|a_{F,u}-a_F-b_F|
+\lVert\phi_{F,u}-\phi_F-u_F\rVert_{C^{2,\vartheta}}
\leq CU_1U_0.
\tag{40}
\]
Applying (40) first to \(p\), using the exact quotient identity for
\(f_{C1}(f_{T0}/f_{C0})\circ p^{-1}\), whose reciprocal and composition remainders are (35) and (38), and then applying (40) to \(T\), yields
\[
\max_{1\leq j\leq J}
\left|
\widetilde T_{P+u}(\widetilde y_j)-\widetilde T_P(\widetilde y_j)
-\mathcal D_P[u]_j
\right|
\leq CU_1U_0.
\tag{41}
\]
Thus the selected lifted nested map is Fr\'echet differentiable, and (41) also gives the quantitative translation-aware remainder requested in the directive.  Notice that branch separation was used only to keep the same smooth squared-distance chart and half-open translation representative.

It remains to verify the covariance orders asserted for \(\mathcal H_P\).  Equations (18)--(19), applied successively to the inner and outer systems and to (26), give a cellwise representation of every coordinate of \(b_p\) and \(b_T\) by a uniformly bounded \(L^2(P_g)\) score.  The elliptic correctors multiplying these two vectors in the corrected \(\mathcal H_P\) have smooth right-hand sides and fixed evaluation points, so energy and interior estimates preserve that bounded-score property.  Applied to a centered kernel tangent, such a functional has score \(K_h^{\mathrm{per}}*\zeta-E(K_h^{\mathrm{per}}*\zeta)(X)\); Young's inequality and ass:density-positivity give a uniform \(L^2(P_g)\) bound.  On the other hand, lem:elliptic-green-gradient-bound, localized to the torus by subtracting the Dirichlet Green function in a coordinate ball and using compactness outside that ball, gives
\[
\lVert\hbox{leading Green score}\rVert_{L^2(P_g)}^2
\leq C\int_h^1r^{-2}r\,dr+C
\leq C\log(1/h).
\tag{42}
\]
Therefore the harmonic variance divided by \(\log(1/h)\) is \(O(1/\log(1/h))\), and Cauchy--Schwarz with (42) makes every normalized Green--harmonic covariance \(O(1/\sqrt{\log(1/h)})\).  All constants are uniform because (3), the density bounds, the two ellipticity assumptions, and ass:lift-regularity are uniform over \(\mathcal F_s\).  This proves the corrected theorem.
